clue.text: Something in the next answer got hermit worried

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters of the two words are fretted and pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a recluse has become anxious about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges GOT HERMIT. The next answer is 6 Across, FAUNA (animal life), and this flying insect is one member of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger moth is a boldly patterned moth, so it is one member of the animal life named in the following solution.

clue.text: Fish trader's case dismissed

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters of the trader's word are used

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A merchant's lawsuit is thrown out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the first and last letters of 'trader's', T and R; 'Case dismissed' reads as a courtroom phrase but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Produces teenagers?

indicators.note: the question mark is the only signal that the letters of the word teenagers should be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what it is that brings young people into being.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no word signalling the anagram: the question mark alone tells you to rearrange TEENAGERS, whose letters exactly match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate something is to bring it into being or create it.

clue.text: The sort of question that makes you a lot richer, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the three words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A quiz question that might win you a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A LOT RICHER; the surface suggests a big-money quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical question is asked for effect, not expecting any reply.

clue.text: African egg producer's a person unable to face reality

definitions.text: a person unable to face reality

explanation.surface: A big African bird is likened to someone who will not face facts.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flightless bird lays enormous eggs, and from the myth that it buries its head in sand, the name also describes someone in denial.

clue.text: Hotel with gold curtains — they'll sting you!

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
or is the heraldic word for gold
net curtains are often just called nets

explanation.surface: A hotel with golden drapes, plus a warning about what lurks there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' looks like part of the hotel description but supplies NETS, as in net curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornets are large wasps with a painful sting.

clue.text: Animal life supporter possessing universal answer

indicators.note: possessing means the supporter word holds the next letter inside itself

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A backer of wildlife holds the answer to everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessing' puts U inside FAN to give FAUN, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the animals of a region or period.

clue.text: Runs into obscure creature

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the word for obscure

parts.note: to fog something is to obscure it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into a mysterious animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective describing the creature but is the verb FOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is an amphibian, one of many creatures in this animal-themed puzzle.

clue.text: Vacates pub, returning distressed

clue.text: Adult realises, accepting notice from people granted authority

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

indicators.note: accepting means the realises word takes the notice word inside it

parts.note: to see a point is to realise it
a sign is a notice

explanation.surface: A grown-up understands who has been given power after reading a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals a container; 'realises' is read as 'sees', as in 'I see what you mean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assignees are those to whom rights, property or duties have been transferred.

clue.text: Weight if start of spring is delayed

indicators.note: start of names the first letter of the word for spring as the one affected
is delayed suggests that first letter arrives too late to be counted and is lost

parts.note: to pounce is to spring on something

explanation.surface: A scale reading that depends on spring coming late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of ... is delayed' drops the P from POUNCE. 'spring' looks like the season but is the verb. The ounce is also the snow leopard, fitting the animal theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small imperial unit of weight, about 28 grams.

clue.text: Shell carriers with nothing in store — it's disastrous

indicators.note: in puts the nothing letter inside the rearranged letters of store and it's
disastrous signals that the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone finds the larder empty and calls it a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges STORE and IT'S into TORTISES, and 'in' places O inside it; the dash makes 'it's disastrous' look like a comment on the empty store.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortoises carry their protective shells on their backs wherever they go.

clue.text: Scares the little brats, conserving one's energy

indicators.note: conserving means the brats word keeps the following letters inside it

parts.note: naughty children are often called little terrors
one is I, so one's gives I plus S
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Mischievous children frighten people while saving their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserving' puts ISE inside TERRORS, between the R and the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To terrorise is to frighten or intimidate.

clue.text: Investor closing theatre early

indicators.note: closing points at the final letter of the theatre word
early says that word finishes before its time, losing that final letter

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: A backer shuts down a show before its run ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing ... early' cuts the last letter from STAGE. A stag is a stock-market speculator who buys new shares to sell them quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag on the stock exchange applies for new share issues hoping to sell at a quick profit.

clue.text: Bans for writers

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
scribes are writers

explanation.surface: Restrictions imposed on authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid or outlaw it.

clue.text: Pet shark or other creature

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
a shark is one kind of fish

explanation.surface: A list of animals: a pet, a shark, or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shark' is an example standing for the general word FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The catfish is a whiskered fish, another creature distinct from the pet and the shark.

clue.text: Accountant with spirit getting leased car

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
brio is spirit or verve
let means leased out

explanation.surface: A lively accountant gets the use of a rented car.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is the British and Commonwealth abbreviation for a chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a convertible.

clue.text: Most of Channel island eat fish

indicators.note: most of means the island name loses its final letter

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: On a British island in the Channel, people eat fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are British islands lying off the coast of France; 'Most of' drops the island's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily fish, usually sold tinned.

clue.text: Promotor of growth from popular island with mounting rubbish

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
Cuba is a Caribbean island

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the rubbish word reads upwards

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: Something that boosts growth comes from a well-liked island with heaps of waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' signals a reversal because in a down light the word is read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator provides warmth and conditions for eggs, premature babies or cultures to develop.

clue.text: A way to chase bankrupt flyer

indicators.note: to chase means to come after, so the following pieces sit behind the bankrupt word

parts.note: a business gone bust is bankrupt
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A road leads off after a ruined man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to chase' means to follow behind, so the pieces after it in the clue come after 'bankrupt' in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large heavy bird that can still fly.

clue.text: Fisherman might have one freely granted

indicators.note: freely says the letters of granted may move about without restriction

explanation.surface: An angler has been given something without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges GRANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a net dragged along the sea bed by a fishing boat.

clue.text: Bugs popular religious cults

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
sects are religious groups or cults

explanation.surface: Popular cults are causing irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' could be a verb meaning annoys, but here it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are often loosely called bugs.

clue.text: Motorway backed up — almost overtook, but no way forward

indicators.note: backed up in a down clue means the motorway name is read upwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 written here as the letter I

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the overtook word is dropped

parts.note: to pass a car is to overtake it

explanation.surface: A traffic jam on the motorway: a driver nearly gets past but is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed up' turns M1 into IM (the 1 read as I); 'almost' cuts PASSED to PASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation with no progress possible.

clue.text: One case of Brie? Ten from this animal!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters of Brie are used

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A cheese lover asks for one box of Brie, but ten come from this beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes B and E from Brie.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns.

clue.text: Former Tory whose time is over?

parts.note: ex means former
Con is short for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A retired Conservative politician whose era has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing time is serving a prison sentence, so 'whose time is over' is a released prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-convict has served a prison sentence and been released.

clue.text: A positive sucker after a night flight?

definitions.text: A positive sucker after a night flight?

parts.words: A positive sucker after a night flight
parts.note: A positive is a blood group, and a creature that sucks blood after flying at night fits the description

explanation.surface: Someone is hungry for blood type A positive after a night of flying.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American creature flies at night and feeds on blood.

clue.text: Cast lose on purpose

explanation.surface: An actor deliberately fluffs their role.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw is to cast, as a ball; to throw a match is to lose it deliberately.

clue.text: Influence wife to get in, for example

indicators.note: to get in means the wife letter goes inside the for example word

parts.note: say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: Persuading your wife to join, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' puts W inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway means power over others, influence.

clue.text: Bugs expert on line extensions

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the expert word follows the line letter

parts.note: an ace is an expert
wings are extensions to a building

explanation.surface: A specialist talks about long lines of extensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places ACE after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacewings are delicate insects with net-veined wings.

clue.text: One may snap, seeing judge releasing the first couple

indicators.note: releasing the first couple means the opening two letters of the judge word go

parts.note: an arbiter is a judge

explanation.surface: A judge frees a pair, and someone reacts angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing the first couple' drops AR from ARBITER. 'couple' suggests a married pair but means two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A biter is something that bites, as a dog does when it snaps.

clue.text: Fish barrel nearly emptied

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

indicators.note: emptied removes all but the first and last letters of nearly

explanation.surface: A barrel of fish is almost empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves N and Y from 'nearly'. 'nearly' looks like it modifies 'emptied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunny is another name for tuna.

clue.text: Creature's disturbed rest here, wailing but not suffering

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
but not means the suffering word is taken away from wailing

parts.note: ailing means suffering

explanation.surface: Someone's sleep is interrupted by wailing, though they are not in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes AILING from WAILING, leaving W; 'disturbed' rearranges REST, HERE and W. A tree shrew is a small squirrel-like Asian mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree shrew is a small tree-dwelling mammal of South-East Asia.
